                                         ble of instruction following and robotic action generation,      cess (MDP) [16, 31], where actions are generated from the

state to preserve historical context and to initialize the current action tokens. Then the AVA module combines this recurrent state with text-

throughout the backbone LLM, enabling the model to focus on task-relevant regions based on both temporal context and current perception.

                                                                  C. Additional Discussions
                                                                  The proposed AVA-VLA framework is different from recent
                                                                  memory-augmented VLA models, such as MemoryVLA
                                                                  [43]. MemoryVLA relies on an explicit, large-scale mem-
                                                                  ory bank for retrieval-based feature augmentation, while
                                                                  AVA-VLA adopts a formal POMDP formulation to com-
                                                                  press historical interactions into a compact, implicit recur-
           Figure 5. AgileX Cobot Magic platforms.                rent state. Moreover, MemoryVLA focuses on augmenting
                                                                  current features with historical tokens, while our AVA-VLA
                                                                  method utilizes the recurrent state to dynamically modulate
B.1. Real-World Task Suites
                                                                  and prune visual tokens at the input level, enabling active
We introduce the detailed specifications for each task suite      visual perception that focuses on task-relevant regions.
in our Mobile ALOHA real-world experiments:                          The significance of temporal modeling and memory

  toy objects of which the instruction has given (yellow ba-      bank architectures in VLN-BERT [13] and SafeVLA [59]
  nana, green pepper, purple eggplant) into the bucket.           or the LSTM-based aggregation in NaVid [60], our ap-
• Dataset: 450 demonstrations (150 per target).                   proach explicitly incorporates a recurrent state based on
• Episode length: 700 timesteps (28 seconds).                     POMDP to enhance visual representations in a simple yet

In this section, we provide additional evidence for three                   suggest that the performance gain mainly comes from the
aspects of AVA-VLA: (i) the gain is not explained by ex-                    proposed architectural synergy between recurrent-state ini-
tra training compute, (ii) the proposed design generalizes                  tialization and active visual attention.
across benchmarks and controlled perturbations, and (iii)
the learned attention is interpretable.                                     D.2. Module Ablation on CALVIN Benchmark

D.4. Effect of the Lω Regularizer
                                                                  horizons, gradually leading to belief drift and failures in
We further analyze the regularization term Lω introduced in       precision-sensitive manipulation such as grasping or place-
Section 3.4 of the main paper. Specifically, we remove the        ment. See the provided qualitative failure cases in Figure
L2 penalty on the soft attention weights while keeping all        13. This issue is especially pronounced in long-horizon
other training settings unchanged. Quantitative results on        tasks such as LIBERO-Long, where performance drops
the LIBERO benchmark are reported in Table 8. Removing            more markedly under visual token reduction. A promising
Lω reduces the average success rate from 98.0% to 97.5%,          direction for future work is to improve the stability of re-
with the most noticeable drop on the LIBERO-Long suite.           current state propagation, for example, through more robust

learned soft attention becomes noticeably more dispersed

Figure 12. Visualization of the soft weights without the regularizer Lω on LIBERO. Compared with the full AVA-VLA result shown
in Figure 4, removing Lω leads to more dispersed attention and increased responses on irrelevant background regions, indicating that the
regularizer helps maintain more selective and structurally robust attention masks.




                            (a) Task: Put the white mug on the plate and put the chocolate pudding to the right of the plate.




                                                      (b) Task: Put both moka pots on the stove.

Figure 13. Failure cases of AVA-VLA on LIBERO. (a) The gripper fails to align with the chocolate pudding due to drifted spatial
belief. (b) A slight positional deviation prevents the robot from securely grasping the moka pot handle. These cases illustrate how minor
perceptual inaccuracies accumulate in the recurrent state, leading to drifted object/contact beliefs and eventual failures in precision-sensitive
long-horizon tasks.
